description: Each case plays one attack of an agent against the stack and names the test that proves the attack fails. Every finding of the AEP 2.9 full code review sits in exactly one place: a case, the open list or the elsewhere list.

cases.attack: Agent B seals a frame whose event names agent A, so the walls would judge A and charge the budget of A.
cases.expect: The binding wall denies the frame and no budget of either agent changes.

cases.attack: An agent sends a frame that Admit allows and the hub permission denies, hoping Apply already changed state.
cases.expect: The live entry stays unchanged and the ledger holds one deny row.

cases.attack: An agent stamps a large frame thirty seconds ahead to become the freeze clock and hold the shared pulse queue.
cases.expect: The kernel refuses the frame at enqueue against its own clock before it takes queue room.

cases.attack: An agent puts a url field into an admitted write so the kernel sends a request for it.
cases.expect: No request leaves the kernel.

cases.attack: An agent sends two frames whose outbound requests hang, to stall the pulse and every collect.
cases.expect: A collect is answered within 500 ms while both slow requests run.

cases.attack: An agent queries a target id that starts with a multi byte character to panic under the live entry lock.
cases.expect: The query is answered and the kernel keeps serving.

cases.attack: A peer without the key of an agent sends frames in its name to spend its rate slots.
cases.expect: A frame with a bad signature spends no rate slot of the agent it names.

cases.attack: An agent fills every connection slot of one dock port to lock the other ports out.
cases.expect: The other ports keep their slots.

cases.attack: An agent opens and ends connections in a loop so the daemon keeps every ended task.
cases.expect: Ended connection tasks are released.

cases.attack: An agent names private, loopback, shared and transition addresses as outbound targets.
cases.expect: Every address and URL vector of the shared vector file gets the verdict it states without a name lookup.

cases.attack: An agent writes a manifest beside its tree, edits its sealed record, copies the record of another draft and renames draft folders.
cases.expect: Each forged record, copied record and renamed folder is refused and no draft lands unscanned.

cases.attack: An agent plants a git config with a filter and a monitor, swaps blob bytes under a scanned id, hides prose behind an invalid byte and commits locally in its draft.
cases.expect: The planted config runs nothing, the swapped blob never lands, the undecodable prose is a finding and exactly one commit lands on the fetched tip.

cases.attack: An agent changes its tree after the scan, hoping promote stages the tree again.
cases.expect: Promote lands the scanned tree object as one commit.

cases.attack: An agent lands a draft whose branch moved after the scan.
cases.expect: The draft needs a new scan and a conflict is refused.

cases.attack: An agent calls a verb on a draft without proving its identity or as an agent whose profile does not grant the verb.
cases.expect: Every verb proves its agent through a signed frame and passes its profile.

cases.attack: An agent sets every variable that once moved the state root, the profile, the forge and the quota to a hostile value.
cases.expect: No verdict changes.

cases.attack: An agent sets the test override of the operator folder against a release build.
cases.expect: A release build reads no control from the environment.

cases.attack: An agent pushes the token of the GitHub forge toward its draft through the git environment of promote.
cases.expect: The push and the pull request run in process with one commit and the token never reaches a file or a git process of the draft.

cases.attack: A writer of the draft ledger edits a field, copies a seal, removes or swaps entries and inserts unsealed entries or stray lines.
cases.expect: The ledger check refuses every change and accepts the untouched ledger.

cases.attack: A writer of the Lattice Memory log changes the bytes of a record.
cases.expect: The store finds the change and never cuts the log at it.

cases.attack: A writer of the Lattice Memory log removes a record or moves one to another place.
cases.expect: The store finds the removed or moved record.

cases.attack: A writer of the Lattice Memory log cuts its tail or replaces the whole log.
cases.expect: The anchor kept outside the store finds the cut or replaced log.

cases.attack: A writer of the Lattice Memory chain changes any one field of an entry.
cases.expect: Every field changes the hash of the entry.

cases.attack: An agent edits a signed UCM receipt to claim another result.
cases.expect: Verification refuses the edited receipt.

cases.attack: The holder of the key of agent A submits frames for agent B through the UCB dock gateway.
cases.expect: The key of A is refused for B.

cases.attack: An agent sends an unsigned manifest that would replace its stored manifest.
cases.expect: The replacement is refused.

cases.attack: An agent signs a manifest with a key that is not registered for it or with no signer.
cases.expect: The signature does not count and the manifest is refused.

cases.attack: An agent with a stored signed manifest uses the egress route.
cases.expect: The digest of the stored manifest matches on egress, so the route does its work.

cases.attack: An agent uses the rollback route, which would send an empty action path that the dock always denies.
cases.expect: The rollback frame names its action path.

cases.attack: An agent sends one ingest that would pass Admit and the ledger twice.
cases.expect: An admitted ingest passes Admit once.

cases.attack: A caller without a key floods the health route to start a child process and a dock frame per request.
cases.expect: Health answers from memory.

cases.attack: An agent repeats one payload below the old replay threshold.
cases.expect: The replay predicate refuses the repeated payload.

cases.attack: A peer presents a mesh certificate long past its stated lifetime.
cases.expect: Issued certificates live no longer than their stated lifetime.

cases.attack: A peer presents an expired client certificate to the dock.
cases.expect: The dock sees the presented certificate and refuses the expired one.

cases.attack: A peer connects so the ledger would name a certificate the dock minted for itself.
cases.expect: The ledger names the certificate the peer presented.

cases.attack: An unknown sender sends datagrams to the mesh packet plane.
cases.expect: A datagram from an unknown sender is dropped.

cases.attack: A peer file lists a mesh peer so health would report the mesh as reachable.
cases.expect: Health reports the mesh only from a bound and authenticated plane.

open.reason: The remediation of these walls is open. Its gate adds one red team case per finding to the multi step corpus of CC-35 and a case here.
The remediation of the UCM limits and receipts is open. Its gate adds the release build programs, the self signed receipt and the depth tests here.

The evidence ledger, the intent ledger and the UCB journal still accept edits outside their hash. Their remediation is open and its gate adds a tamper case per ledger field and a cut ledger case here.

open.area: Scanners, model gateway, graph engine and observers
open.reason: The remediation of the scanners, the gateway, the graph engine and the observers is open. Its gate adds the timing, key format, stream and graph cases here.
Hygiene of the container, the toolchain, the lock files and the build order of the tests. No agent plays these. Their remediation is open.
Findings of the follow-up reading in the policy builders, the registry, the plan generator, the scanners and the user experience harness that are open or fixed in part. Their tickets add the cases.

elsewhere.reason: These findings name the Go CAW, which left the tree. Host sandbox enforcement of the CAW that ships is proven by AEP-CAWs-RustGvisor/proof/hostile-corpus.sh in the caw-gvisor job.
LEAD 01 is proven by the tests of aep-tla-verify, LEAD 02 by the script coverage test of the root vitest run and LEAD 03 by this corpus and the end to end job of the base-node workflow.
Fixed with the script tests of the policy builders, the registry, the universal connect client and the user experience harness, which the root vitest run holds.
